definitions.explanation: A comprehensive collection of all or most works by a single author, artist, or on a single subject, typically published as a multi-volume set.

examples.japanese: {夏目漱石|なつめそうせき}{全集|ぜんしゅう}を{読|よ}んでいる。
examples.english: I am reading the complete works of Natsume Soseki.

examples.japanese: {全集|ぜんしゅう}は{全|ぜん}20{巻|かん}で{構成|こうせい}されている。
examples.english: The collected works are composed of 20 volumes.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{書斎|しょさい}には{世界文学全集|せかいぶんがくぜんしゅう}がずらりと{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: In my grandfather's study, a complete collection of world literature was lined up on the shelves.

notes:
Composed of {全|ぜん} (complete, all) + {集|しゅう} (collection). Commonly used in the titles of multi-volume publications.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{著作|ちょさく}{全集|ぜんしゅう} (complete written works)
・{全集|ぜんしゅう}を{刊行|かんこう}する (publish a complete works)
・{全|ぜん}○{巻|かん}の{全集|ぜんしゅう} (a complete works in ○ volumes)
